The total vol- ume of fluid, which is determined by the patient’s body-weight, should be infused over about 4 hours. The infusion rate should be increased gradually: the initial rate should not exceed 1 mg/kg per hour; once the patient can tolerate this rate, it may be in- creased every 30 minutes by 2 mg/kg per hour with monitoring of vital signs before each increase; the maximum infusion rate is 7 mg/kg per hour. Infusion reactions are common with alglucosidase alfa; symp- toms may resolve on decreasing the infusion rate, temporarily stopping the infusion, and/or use of antihistamines and/or antipy- retics, which may also be given as pre-treatment. Severe reac- tions may require stopping the infusion immediately. Serious hy- persensitivity reactions, including anaphylactic shock, have also been reported during infusion of alglucosidase alfa. ◊ References. 1. Amalfitano A, et al.
